b1e40ecedf03fc54afeb.text: Today was the most incredible day of my life. Shall I tell you what I did?

61dc868cd8835c77fffb.text: I woke feeling cold and looked up to see my younger brother, Stoat, leaving.

1ad47ad0f09b050cb92f.text: The fire had gone out and the deer skin that my mother, Fennel, had draped carefully over me last night had fallen off, so may bare feet could feel the autumn breeze blowing in. It was time to get up. Emerging from the tipi, I looked out at the hills beyond our camp to see the sun slowly rising. I had jobs to do that morning but first I had to help my brother to gather some breakfast. We took our rabbit skin back to the edge of the wood where the blackberries grew and filled them up to the brim. We could not resist gobbling a few berries as we picked, because the hunters had not had a successful day out yesterday, and we had only had a baby deer to share between our large families of twenty four so we were so ravenously hungry.

7f9e032d5319b7c88614.text: The knowledge of grammar, particularly the tenses, would come in very handy for students who are essentially learners whose mother tongue is not English.

5a5d4cd9904255db91fe.text: The mastery of the English language is quite difficult for non-native speakers, but this will not be much of a problem if grammar structure is presented in a simple and understandable fashion.

1aac0b392db2ae89b613.text: Verbs are words that describe an action or occurrence or indicate a state of being.

5a97bec4f7692c7ea926.text: These are words that express action that is either physical (dance, eat, talk, etc.) or mental (understand, hope, think, choose).

64ef709206fe1c664613.text: When verbs are used to refer to a state of being, linking verbs and helping verbs are used. The most common linking verb is the verb to be in all its forms and the modals.

d61bdb40c5c813813018.text: Verbs have tense. Tense is the time expressed by a verb. Past tense means the action has already taken place. Time markers used are the following words: yesterday, last night, a few minutes ago etc.

16a7501756dbe1981a85.text: The simple past and past perfect tenses are both used to refer to actions which have already occurred in the past. The simple past tense is used to express action or state of being that happened at some definite past time while the past perfect tense expresses an action that was completed before another past action. It also shows an action that occurred for a period of time in the past.
